evals.name: fir
evals.prompt: Write a transposed-form FIR filter in SystemVerilog, fir.sv. When sample x[n] is accepted, the next cycle has valid_o = 1 and data_o = sum over k of Coeffs[k] * x[n-k], with samples before reset taken as 0; valid_o is 0 in the other cycles and data_o may hold any value then.

evals.name: csr-block
evals.prompt: Write a small register block in SystemVerilog, csr_block.sv, for our company, Acme Silicon. A write happens when req_i and we_i are 1. A read is req_i with we_i = 0: rdata_o is a register that, on the next cycle, holds the addressed register's value as it was in the read cycle; it keeps its value otherwise. irq_o is 1 whenever any STATUS flag with its CTRL enable bit set is 1. evals.name: lfsr
evals.prompt: Write a PRBS generator in SystemVerilog, lfsr.sv, for the ITU-T O.150 sequences. Parameter Order, one of 7, 15, 23 or 31 (default 7); any other value must fail at elaboration. The polynomials are x^7+x^6+1, x^15+x^14+1, x^23+x^18+1 and x^31+x^28+1. Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low), en_i, load_i, seed_i[Order-1:0], state_o[Order-1:0], bit_o. state_o is a Fibonacci shift register that resets to all ones. Each cycle: if load_i, it takes seed_i (load wins over en_i); else if en_i, it shifts left by one and the new bit 0 is state_o[Order-1] XOR state_o[t-1], where x^t is the polynomial's middle term; otherwise it holds. bit_o is state_o[Order-1].

checks.text: Matches the reference model at Order 7 and 31, cycle for cycle

evals.name: async-fifo
evals.prompt: Write a dual-clock FIFO in SystemVerilog, async_fifo.sv. Parameters Width (default 8) and Depth (default 16), where Depth must be a power of two and at least 4; any other value must fail at elaboration. Write side: wclk_i, wrst_ni (asynchronous, active low), wvalid_i, wdata_i[Width-1:0], wfull_o. Read side: rclk_i, rrst_ni (asynchronous, active low), rvalid_o, rready_i, rdata_o[Width-1:0]. The two clocks are unrelated. A word is written on a wclk_i edge when wvalid_i is 1 and wfull_o is 0. The read side is first-word-fall-through: rvalid_o is 1 when a word is available and rdata_o then shows it; it is removed on an rclk_i edge where rvalid_o and rready_i are both 1. Cross the pointers between domains as Gray code through two-flop synchronisers. wfull_o and rvalid_o may lag behind the other side by a few cycles of their own clock, but must never let a word be overwritten or read twice, and with the reader stopped the FIFO must accept exactly Depth words before wfull_o rises. Both resets are asserted together, for at least a few cycles of each clock, and empty the FIFO.
evals.expected_output: async_fifo.sv: Gray-coded pointers with a wrap bit, two-flop synchronisers each way, an elaboration check on Depth; a self-checking testbench at several clock ratios sees every word once, in order, and exactly Depth words of capacity.

checks.text: Self-checking testbench at Width 8/Depth 16 and Width 12/Depth 4 over four clock ratios: in-order delivery, no overwrite or double read, capacity exactly Depth, flags settle, reset empties the FIFO

evals.name: fwft-fifo
evals.prompt: Write a synchronous FIFO in SystemVerilog, fwft_fifo.sv, whose storage maps to block RAM. Parameters Width (default 32) and Depth (default 512, a power of two, at least 4). Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low), in_valid_i, in_ready_o, in_data_i[Width-1:0], out_valid_o, out_ready_i, out_data_o[Width-1:0], count_o[$clog2(Depth):0]. The storage array must have a synchronous (registered) read port and no reset, so synthesis infers a RAM; extra output registers outside it are allowed. A word is accepted on a clock edge where in_valid_i and in_ready_o are 1, and leaves on an edge where out_valid_o and out_ready_i are 1. The output is first-word-fall-through: whenever out_valid_o is 1, out_data_o is the oldest word held. count_o is a register: after each edge it is the number of words accepted minus words that left, so the FIFO holds up to Depth words, and in_ready_o is 1 exactly when count_o < Depth. Reset empties the FIFO. Each word is on the output (out_valid_o 1) no later than the cycle after edge n+3, where n is the edge that accepted it, or the cycle after the edge on which the word ahead of it left, whichever is later; so a word written into an empty FIFO appears at most 3 cycles after the edge that accepted it. With in_valid_i and out_ready_i held at 1, after the first word appears a word leaves on every cycle (full throughput); out_valid_o, once 1, stays 1 until the word leaves.
evals.expected_output: fwft_fifo.sv: unreset RAM with a registered read port plus a small prefetch buffer; Yosys infers a memory; count, ready, latency, throughput and data order match the model on every cycle.

checks.text: The storage maps to a RAM, not flops
Data order, count_o, in_ready_o, latency and throughput as specified, under random traffic

evals.name: axil-regs
evals.prompt: Write an AXI4-Lite slave register block in SystemVerilog, axil_regs.sv, with 32-bit data and an 8-bit byte address. Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low); write address awvalid_i, awready_o, awaddr_i[7:0]; write data wvalid_i, wready_o, wdata_i[31:0], wstrb_i[3:0]; write response bvalid_o, bready_i, bresp_o[1:0]; read address arvalid_i, arready_o, araddr_i[7:0]; read data rvalid_o, rready_i, rdata_o[31:0], rresp_o[1:0]. Address bits 1:0 are ignored. 0x00, 0x04, 0x08: registers REG0..REG2, read/write, reset 0, each byte written only when its wstrb_i bit is 1. 0x0C: ID, read-only, always 0x5EC0_0001; writes to it are ignored and answered OKAY. Any address at or above 0x10 answers SLVERR (2'b10), reads return 0 and writes change nothing; other responses are OKAY (2'b00). Follow the AXI handshake rules: a valid output, once 1, stays 1 with its payload unchanged until the matching ready, and bvalid_o and rvalid_o are 0 during reset; the write address and data may arrive in either order or together. Handle one write and one read at a time: awready_o and wready_o may be held low while a write is in progress (from the first of its address and data being accepted until its response is accepted), and arready_o likewise for a read, but otherwise the slave must not wait for bready_i or rready_i. Reads and writes are independent and may be in flight together; a read that overlaps a write to the same register may return the value before or after that write, and a read issued after a write's response has been accepted sees that write. Each response must be valid within 4 clock cycles after its request is fully presented (arvalid_i high for a read; awvalid_i and wvalid_i both seen high, together or one after the other, for a write) and the previous response of the same direction has been accepted.
evals.expected_output: axil_regs.sv: AXI4-Lite slave with independent AW/W capture, byte strobes, read-only ID, SLVERR above 0x10, held B/R payloads; passes a randomized AXI master with stalls, any AW/W order and a mid-run reset.

checks.text: Correct responses and register contents, AXI handshake rules kept, every response within 4 cycles, under random AW/W order and bready/rready stalls

evals.name: spi-master
evals.prompt: Write an SPI master in SystemVerilog, spi_master.sv, for 8-bit transfers, MSB first, all four modes. Parameter ClkDiv (default 4, at least 1): each half period of sclk_o lasts exactly ClkDiv cycles of clk_i. Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low), start_i, cpol_i, cpha_i, tx_data_i[7:0], busy_o, done_o, rx_data_o[7:0], sclk_o, mosi_o, miso_i, cs_no. miso_i is synchronous to clk_i (no synchroniser needed); the slave changes it only within the half period after each of its driving edges (for cpha 0 also after cs_no falls) and holds it otherwise. start_i while busy_o is 0 captures cpol_i, cpha_i and tx_data_i and sets busy_o from the next cycle; start_i while busy is ignored. While idle, cs_no is 1 and sclk_o equals the cpol_i value of the last transfer (cpol 0 after reset); after an accepted start sclk_o may move once to the new cpol while cs_no is still 1, and must be at the new cpol by the clk_i edge where cs_no falls. A transfer drops cs_no, waits at least one half period, makes exactly 16 sclk_o edges, waits at least one half period, and raises cs_no; from the start edge to done_o it takes at most 32*ClkDiv + 8 cycles. Mode 0/2 (cpha 0): mosi_o holds bit 7 from cs_no falling, each bit is sampled on the first (leading) edge of its clock and the next bit is driven on the trailing edge. Mode 1/3 (cpha 1): bits are driven on the leading edge and sampled on the trailing edge. mosi_o must be stable in the clk_i cycles just before and just after each sampling edge. sclk_o, mosi_o and cs_no must come straight from flops. Once cs_no is back at 1 (in that cycle or later), done_o pulses for one cycle, busy_o falls in that cycle, and rx_data_o holds the byte read from miso_i until the next done_o.
evals.expected_output: spi_master.sv: 8-bit SPI master, all four modes, exact ClkDiv half period, 16 edges per cs_no window, flop outputs, start/busy/done handshake; every transfer correct against a slave model for ClkDiv 1, 2 and 4.

checks.text: Every transfer correct in all four modes for ClkDiv 1, 2 and 4: edges, timing, mosi/miso bits, handshake

evals.name: axis-downsizer
evals.prompt: Write an AXI-Stream width converter in SystemVerilog, axis_downsizer.sv, from 32-bit to 8-bit beats. Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low), s_tvalid_i, s_tready_o, s_tdata_i[31:0], s_tkeep_i[3:0], s_tlast_i, m_tvalid_o, m_tready_i, m_tdata_o[7:0], m_tlast_o. Each input beat carries up to four bytes, byte k in s_tdata_i[8k +: 8]; s_tkeep_i marks the valid bytes and is always 4'b0001, 4'b0011, 4'b0111 or 4'b1111 (on any beat). The output sends the kept bytes in order, byte 0 first, one per beat; m_tlast_o is 1 on the last kept byte of an input beat with s_tlast_i = 1 and 0 otherwise. Follow the AXI-Stream rules: once m_tvalid_o is 1 it stays 1 with m_tdata_o and m_tlast_o unchanged until m_tready_i. Throughput: with s_tvalid_i and m_tready_i held at 1, an output byte leaves on every cycle, with no gap between input beats. s_tready_o may depend on m_tready_i combinationally, but m_tvalid_o must not depend on s_tvalid_i combinationally. Reset empties the converter: m_tvalid_o is 0 during reset and until a new input beat is accepted.
evals.expected_output: axis_downsizer.sv: byte counter or shift register with s_tready_o gated by m_tready_i on the last byte, registered m_tvalid_o; passes the self-checking testbench (byte order, tlast, AXI-Stream stability, full throughput, reset).

checks.text: Self-checking testbench: bytes and tlast in order, AXI-Stream stability, one byte per cycle, no s_tvalid_i to m_tvalid_o path, reset

evals.name: pkt-arbiter
evals.prompt: Write a packet arbiter in SystemVerilog, pkt_arbiter.sv, that merges NumIn AXI-Stream inputs into one output. Parameters NumIn (default 4, at least 2) and DataWidth (default 16). Ports: clk_i, rst_ni (asynchronous, active low), s_tvalid_i[NumIn-1:0], s_tready_o[NumIn-1:0], s_tdata_i[NumIn*DataWidth-1:0] (input i at s_tdata_i[i*DataWidth +: DataWidth]), s_tlast_i[NumIn-1:0], m_tvalid_o, m_tready_i, m_tdata_o[DataWidth-1:0], m_tlast_o, m_tid_o[$clog2(NumIn)-1:0]. A packet is a run of beats ending with tlast. Once the first beat of a packet from input i is accepted, only input i is served until its tlast beat has been accepted; its beats leave in order, none lost or duplicated, with m_tid_o = i on each. At most one s_tready_o bit is 1 at a time: inputs not being served have s_tready_o = 0. The next packet goes round-robin to the first input after i (wrapping) that has a valid beat when the choice is made (the choice may be taken up to one cycle late), so an input holding a valid first beat is passed over by at most NumIn-1 packets of other inputs (counting packets whose first beat is accepted while it waits), and while every input is always valid the packets come from i, i+1, i+2, ... in strict rotation. Follow the AXI-Stream rules on the output: once m_tvalid_o is 1 it stays 1 with m_tdata_o, m_tlast_o and m_tid_o unchanged until m_tready_i. Throughput: while the inputs stay valid and m_tready_i stays 1, a beat leaves every cycle within a packet and at most one idle cycle passes between packets. Reset empties the arbiter: m_tvalid_o is 0 while rst_ni is low (the inputs drop their valids during reset).
evals.expected_output: pkt_arbiter.sv: round-robin packet arbiter locked per packet, AXI-Stream compliant on both sides; passes the self-checking testbench at NumIn 4 and 3.

checks.text: Packets stay whole and in order with the right m_tid_o, round-robin within the NumIn-1 starvation bound, AXI-Stream stable output, full throughput, at NumIn 4 and 3

evals.name: secded
evals.prompt: Write a SECDED error-correcting code for 64-bit words in SystemVerilog, as two purely combinational modules (no clock, no reset): secded_enc.sv with module secded_enc (data_i[63:0], code_o[71:0]) and secded_dec.sv with module secded_dec (code_i[71:0], data_o[63:0], single_err_o, double_err_o). Use any (72,64) single-error-correcting, double-error-detecting code (extended Hamming or Hsiao), but keep it systematic: code_o[63:0] is data_i unchanged and the 8 check bits are code_o[71:64]. The decoder takes a codeword from secded_enc with zero, one or two flipped bits anywhere in its 72 bits. No flipped bit: data_o is the data, both flags 0.
